request.event_title: Iran war escalation affecting FUJIFILM executive management
request.event_description: Iran war escalation may disrupt sanctions screening, Middle East shipping routes, energy prices, supplier continuity, payments, and executive-level decisions for FUJIFILM healthcare, electronics, imaging, and business innovation operations.

selected_candidates.title: Executive decision paralysis from geopolitical uncertainty
selected_candidates.description: Iran war escalation creates cascading uncertainty across FUJIFILM's diversified operations — healthcare, electronics, imaging, and business innovation — potentially delaying or derailing executive-level strategic decisions on capital allocation, M&A, and market expansion. Energy price volatility and sanctions complexity compound decision-making risk at the executive tier.
selected_candidates.rationale: Direct scope match: The event explicitly affects executive management. The scope is defined as 'FUJIFILM Executive Management' in the Executive department, making strategic decision disruption the most directly relevant risk to this scope.

selected_candidates.title: Sanctions compliance breach via Iranian supplier and payment channels
selected_candidates.description: Escalation of Iran war increases risk of inadvertent sanctions violations through existing supplier relationship with Tehran Medical Service Partner (SUP-FJ-IR-001), a high-criticality supplier with no alternative available, and pending USD payment of $2.4M routed through a Tehran correspondent bank. Sanctions clauses exist in contract CTR-FJ-IR-9001 but enforcement under active conflict is uncertain.
scope_matches: FUJIFILM healthcare operations dependent on Iranian medical service parts
selected_candidates.rationale: Direct scope match: Executive management is responsible for sanctions compliance and supplier continuity. The Iranian supplier is high-criticality with no alternative, and a pending payment exists through an Iranian bank — both directly threatened by Iran war escalation.

selected_candidates.title: Middle East logistics disruption to healthcare supply chain
selected_candidates.description: Iran war escalation disrupts Middle East shipping routes, directly impacting Gulf Logistics Corridor (SUP-FJ-GULF-002), a high-criticality UAE-based supplier providing cold-chain and spare-parts logistics for FUJIFILM healthcare operations in Japan. While an alternative is available, rerouting and contract transition under active conflict could cause significant delays to medical systems field-service operations.
scope_matches: Executive oversight of supply chain resilience
selected_candidates.rationale: Direct scope match: Executive management must ensure healthcare supply continuity. The UAE logistics supplier is critical to medical systems service delivery, and war escalation in Iran directly threatens adjacent Middle East shipping corridors.
